_doc: Bounds on what the scheduled reconcile is allowed to re-ship. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-ship-reconcile-reship.sh. These are the operator's safety knobs for #354 and they live here, not inside the script, so raising or lowering the fleet's auto-repair aggression is a data edit.
_doc_reship_classes: Which cloud-ship-reconcile.sh finding classes get automatically re-shipped. `drift` (running digest != registry digest) is the #354 signature and is always safe to re-ship: the deploy is idempotent and the service was ALREADY meant to be at that digest. `absent` and `unpublished` are deliberately excluded — nine services read absent on the fleet for reasons that are not #354 (retired, on-demand, run outside compose), and auto-shipping them would hold the single WG runner to fix nothing. They are reported for a human instead. `created` (#560) IS re-shipped: a declared container that exists but never started is a deploy that was cut short — the same #354 mechanism — and the deploy's down+up is exactly the repair. `stopped` (exited/dead/paused, not a declared one_shot) is NOT: a crashed long-runner is not fixed by re-deploying the same image, and re-shipping it every run would hold the WG lock to fix nothing.
_doc_max_reships_per_run: Hard cap on services dispatched by ONE reconcile run. The re-ship runs on ship-wg-runner, the fleet's single deploy lock, and #179 is the standing reminder of what a long hold on that lock costs: cgc-db index jobs held it for up to 5.5 hours and every deploy behind them was evicted. An uncapped reconcile finding 40 drifted services would reproduce exactly that outage while believing it was repairing one. 5 services is roughly 15-50 minutes of lock, inside the deploy job's 90-minute ceiling with room to spare. The remainder is NOT lost: it is reported, and the next scheduled reconcile picks it up, because a reconcile converges by repetition rather than by finishing in one pass.
